feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the public-sector specialization comes through well. It is generally well written, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and opportunities to sharpen impact through clearer outcomes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into senior ownership of web, analytics, governance, multimedia, and digital strategy.  
- Good credibility signals: specific platforms, tools, scale metrics, and concrete projects make the profile believable and relevant.  
- Professional, polished tone: language is confident and aligned to senior communications/platform roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition and tighten structure: “digital strategy / governance / workflows / content operations” appears frequently across summary, competencies, skills, and roles. Consolidate overlapping sections, especially Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than business results. Include clearer impact such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix minor style inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs “organization’s,” mixed punctuation in bullets, and title casing such as “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning).” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it reads slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it around scale, public-sector relevance, and leadership outcomes would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger leadership language like “leading” or “driving” to sound more executive.
- Add one concrete scale signal from recent experience, e.g. “10,000+ page web ecosystems” or “high-volume, multi-stakeholder communications.”
- Simplify the service list to 3–4 priority areas: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds and scales digital platforms, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, and AI-enabled discovery experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with footer project examples and core competencies; “AI-enabled discovery experiences” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” is somewhat repetitive with the subtitle and competencies section.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with tighter, parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use concise, parallel noun phrases and remove filler like “operations” where possible.
- Emphasize the most marketable and recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search.
- Consider this version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- Standardize style: spell out “and” instead of mixing with “&” for a more polished, consistent tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming either this block or the Topline Skills categories.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with multiple experience bullets and the header.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a compressed repeat of the recent consulting and NACo experience. Tightening phrasing and making the formatting more scannable will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short lead-in such as “Selected Recent Projects” and format each item as a clean bullet with a title plus one concise outcome-focused line.
- Standardize style: use parallel verbs, consistent punctuation, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV consistency.
- Increase specificity where possible with scale, audience, or purpose: e.g., “legislative search,” “Drupal 10 microsite,” “conference installation,” “recurring advocacy series.”
- Trim filler phrases like “designed for continued campaign growth” to sharper wording such as “built for reuse and expansion.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with the current freelance role and NACo bullets.
- The anniversary campaign may add the most distinct value because it introduces experiential/display work not emphasized elsewhere.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads broad and overlaps with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around strategic scope, technical leadership, and 1–2 concrete outcomes or scale indicators.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Lead digital strategy, Drupal platform development, and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, improving enterprise web experiences and campaign delivery.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 impact-led bullets; start with strong verbs: “Built,” “Led,” “Advised,” “Developed,” “Improved.”
- Add measurable context where possible: number of sites/pages/users, team/stakeholder groups supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements.
- Rephrase for concision: combine “digital systems, workflows and analytics” + “governance, usability and operational best practices” into one bullet on enterprise communications operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” overlaps with the Recent Projects “AI Hybrid Search”; keep this entry high-level and leave technical detail to the project section.
- Drupal microsites/toolkits/storytelling also overlaps with “We Are Counties Microsite”; avoid repeating the same examples verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with highest-impact wins: website migration, analytics stack, in-house studio, governance/operations.
- Make channel bullet more outcome-driven or cut it if metrics are limited; e.g., “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials, aligning distribution with advocacy and member engagement goals.”
- Tighten phrasing: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version focused on enterprise leadership and systems.
- Video/programming language also echoes earlier NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and expanding organizational capacity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before the larger platform/governance work in the next role.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and measurable if possible: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper point: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” echo the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; keep this entry focused on scaling/operationalizing, not originating.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tightened to emphasize senior leadership scope and avoid generic phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Audience-centered messaging for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider dropping “Audience-focused content planning” unless you can make it more distinctive, e.g. “Content strategy aligned to user needs and organizational goals.”
- Keep terms that reinforce recent leadership-level work; “public-sector and advocacy messaging” is stronger than broad “content leadership.”
- If space allows, use parallel noun phrases and avoid mixing broad capabilities with tactical activities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” also overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and Core Competencies. Make it more selective and outcome-oriented, emphasizing recent strengths in Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older platforms unless required by the target role; keep WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages only if they are job-relevant.
- Drop “jQuery” unless specifically requested; it dates the profile and adds little versus JavaScript.
- If space allows, add scale cues tied to recent work, e.g., “Drupal modernization for 10,000+ page, high-traffic public-sector sites.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Platform/tool lists duplicate the “Technical + IT” section; keep this section higher-level.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize higher-value analytical leadership and decision support, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line: “Analytics infrastructure & decision support: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Replace generic items with sharper outcomes-oriented phrasing: change “KPI design” to “KPI framework development” and “Leadership reporting” to “executive dashboards and leadership reporting”
- Make “SEO and performance analysis” more precise: use “SEO, UX and content performance analysis”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics infrastructure & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework development • Executive dashboards and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and content performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave fuller platform lists to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and higher-value production capabilities rather than basic tasks.

Suggested edit
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level wording: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio buildout and operations,” “PTZ/multi-camera production systems.”
- Consider a tighter rewrite: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ and multi-camera systems • Studio operations and production workflows”
- If accurate, add scale/outcome language in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., number of events, recurring programs, or in-house studio launched.
- Drop “video editing” unless you want to signal hands-on execution; at your level, “production” and “operations” read stronger.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid near-identical wording here.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; combine them to save space.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/recency: Drupal first, then WordPress/SharePoint; keep GitHub Pages last as a lighter-use tool.
- Consider adding version/scope only where strongest, e.g., “Drupal 9/10” or “SharePoint intranet/content management,” if accurate.
- Keep naming consistent: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills: “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Consider removing one list or making this one more technical/specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles/projects; avoid overloading multiple sections with the same platform names.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more implementation-focused and trim older/basic terms unless they support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize applied capability: “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation” or “Web Development & Integrations.”
- Reorder by relevance to recent work: “JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • HTML5 • CSS3 • jQuery”
- If accurate, replace broad items with stronger specifics tied to recent projects: e.g., “JavaScript (front-end enhancements) • API integrations • GTM implementation • Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting) • GitHub Actions (deployment automation)”
- Consider dropping versioned/basic labels (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) and keeping “HTML, CSS” for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid adding similar automation language here unless you remove overlap in other sections.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already highlighted elsewhere. Make it tighter and more role-relevant by grouping tools by function and emphasizing automation platforms over general collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Automation & Workflow Systems: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira/Asana/Trello • Slack/Teams
- Put highest-signal tools first: lead with Airtable, Power Automate, and Zapier since they best support your workflow automation positioning.
- Consolidate similar PM tools to save space: use “Jira/Asana/Trello” rather than listing each separately.
- Consider dropping Basecamp unless it was materially used in recent roles; it feels less relevant than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so avoid overloading this section with the same emphasis.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if you want to signal operational coordination, not technical depth.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since recent roles emphasize enterprise email/newsletter operations, this item should signal level of use and audience/communications context.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (enterprise email marketing, newsletter operations, audience engagement)
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses: “used to support newsletters and member communications reaching tens of thousands of stakeholders”
- Keep only platforms you used meaningfully in recent roles; order by strongest/recentest experience, likely Higher Logic or Dynamics 365 first if applicable

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating the same audience metric here unless adding platform-specific context
- “Engagement” is broad and may duplicate “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies unless clarified as email/member platforms

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” As a Technical + IT item, it should skew more tool-specific and less conceptual.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to platforms + methods: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • Dashboard development”
- Replace broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding” with more concrete phrasing: “Google Search Console” / “SEO analysis” and “Dashboard development.”
- If truthful, add one implementation tool to increase technical credibility, e.g. “Google Tag Manager” (though it currently sits in Coding & Technical Implementation).
- Consider retitling to “Analytics & Optimization Tools” for cleaner alignment with the content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” Keep this version tool-led and leave KPI/reporting language in Topline Skills.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role; avoid expanding this list with narrative claims here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, site refresh support, and multimedia production.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution level: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social, and multimedia operations.”
- Split the second sentence into concrete achievements: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “coordinating work with a digital media associate” unless you directly managed them.
- Add metrics if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email volume, or workflow time saved.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this item focused on launching/producing the series, not expanding it.
- Avoid repeating broad workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the 2018–2024 NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes or scope, while avoiding overlap with later multimedia/digital production roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize the standout achievement first: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer contribution: “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audiences served, internal stakeholders supported, or types of projects delivered.
- Keep this entry focused on innovation/research + podcast launch, not broader digital operations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here unless this role truly owned it.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to tool proficiency only and keep the strongest, most current production capabilities elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Creative Tools” or “Media Production Tools” to avoid mixing tools with workflows.
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator”
- If you want one capability included, make it more specific: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production”
- Only keep “Podcast production” here if no stronger, outcome-based podcast mention appears in experience; otherwise move it to an older role bullet.
